title: Bennett v. Missouri Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC held Case 2012-09 administratively out of order for lack of standing; it reached no merits determination. Vote: 15 concurring, 2 dissenting, 1 disqualified, 1 not qualified, 1 recused, 4 absent.
first_summary: The SJC held TE M. Jay Bennett’s complaint against Missouri Presbytery administratively out of order because he lacked standing, having been received into the OPC before filing with the SJC. The vote was 15 concurring, 2 dissenting, 1 disqualified, 1 not qualified, 1 recused, and 4 absent. No merits ruling or dissent rationale is stated.
summary: The SJC held TE M. Jay Bennett’s complaint against Missouri Presbytery administratively out of order for lack of standing. Bennett was a PCA member when he complained to Presbytery on April 16, 2012, but was received by the OPC on April 28, 2012; when he filed with the SJC on August 16, 2012, he was no longer a PCA member. The SJC reached no merits issue. The vote was 15 concurring, 2 dissenting, 1 disqualified, 1 not qualified, 1 recused, and 4 absent; no dissent rationale is stated.
